composition.story: Six points lie on a number line at 1, 2, 4, 9, 11 and 12. K-means with k=2 places two centroids, assigns each point to its nearest centroid, moves each centroid to its group's mean, and repeats until nothing changes. Compare two starting positions.

aha.observation: When every point sits with its nearest centroid and each centroid is its group's mean, another loop changes nothing, so k-means stops.

controls.label: Step
controls.presentation: Previous / Next buttons; keyboard arrow keys

controls.label: Starting centroids
controls.presentation: Selects the variant; changes the starting centroids and the number of loops needed

controls.label: Reset
controls.presentation: Returns to the first step and default starting centroids

states.label: Six points
states.sentence: Six points sit on a number line at 1, 2, 4, 9, 11 and 12. We want k = 2 groups.
states.why: Point C at 4 is the one whose group is least obvious.

states.label: Place centroids
states.sentence: Pick two starting centroids on data points: c1 at 1 and c2 at 2. Both start in the left group.
states.why: A poor start lets us see how the loop repairs itself.

states.label: Assign (1st)
states.sentence: Each point joins its nearest centroid. Only A goes to c1; B, C, D, E and F all go to c2.
states.why: Point C is 3 from c1 but only 2 from c2.

states.label: Update (1st)
states.sentence: Each centroid moves to the mean of its points. c1 stays at 1; c2 jumps to (2+4+9+11+12)/5 = 7.6.
states.why: The mean of a lopsided group sits far from the old centroid: c2 moved 5.6.

states.label: Assign (2nd)
states.sentence: With c2 at 7.6, points A, B and C are now nearer c1. D, E and F stay with c2.
states.why: C is 3.0 from c1 but 3.6 from c2, so it switches.

states.label: Update (2nd)
states.why: Each centroid now sits at the center of its own group.

states.label: Assign (3rd)
states.sentence: Re-checking every point against the new centroids, nobody changes group. C is 1.67 from c1 and 6.67 from c2.
states.why: No switch means the next update cannot move any centroid.

states.label: Converged
states.sentence: Updating again gives the same means, so the centroids stop moving. Assign and update have nothing left to change.
states.why: Each loop never raises total squared distance, so with no changes the algorithm stops.

states.label: Six points
states.sentence: Six points sit on a number line at 1, 2, 4, 9, 11 and 12. We want k = 2 groups.
states.why: Point C at 4 is the one whose group is least obvious.

states.label: Place centroids
states.sentence: Pick two starting centroids on data points: c1 at 2 and c2 at 11, one in each apparent group.
states.why: A spread-out start should need fewer loops than the close start.

states.label: Assign (1st)
states.sentence: A, B and C are nearest c1; D, E and F are nearest c2. C is 2 from c1 and 7 from c2.
states.why: The first assignment already matches the natural groups.

states.label: Update (1st)
states.sentence: Centroids move to the group means: c1 = 7/3 = 2.33 and c2 = 32/3 = 10.67.
states.why: Both centroids shift slightly toward the center of their points.

states.label: Assign (2nd)
states.sentence: Checking every point against the moved centroids, nobody changes group. C is still nearer c1.
states.why: No switch means the next update cannot move any centroid.

states.label: Converged
states.sentence: Updating again leaves the centroids where they are. Converged after one update, because the start was good.
states.why: Same final groups as the close start, reached in fewer loops.
